note: Rendered contrast measured off real screenshots of the running guide, against what Model's contrast arithmetic predicts for the same case. This exists because a single earlier measurement was read as proof that the model was wrong by 1.25 ratio points, and a design was refused on that basis. It was not the model that was wrong: the old pass measured the failure GLYPH, drawn at opacity 0.8, and compared it against a value computed for the 0.52 text rung. See docs/UX-GUIDE-AT-SCALE.md section 16.
method: grim capture of the live shell with the guide open, the modal colour of a tight crop taken as the background, and the single most-contrasting pixel in that crop taken as the fully-covered glyph stroke. Repeated on a second capture; identical to two decimals both times.
capturedAtNote: Rows carry the date they were captured and, since F-CAL-3, the environment too -- read `env`, never the date, to know which rendering a row describes, because 2026-09-21 spans BOTH. That day's segment A was the live pass and produced every caption and glyph row; its segment C was headless cage and produced only the four bold-caption rows. The 2026-09-22 rows are the longest-string re-measure under cage, plus the live bold-caption and live control rows added when F-CAL-3 was fixed. The retropc rows predate all of it and were live. The caption rows are a BEFORE state, since D-RUNG-14 made four of those sites bold.
toleranceNote: Every measurement lands BELOW its predicted value, never above, because even the peak pixel of 10px text is not always fully covered. The model is therefore slightly OPTIMISTIC, which is why a target must sit above 4.5 and never on it.
sizeClassNote: F-CAL-1, lead's ruling 2026-09-21: the model's error is size-dependent, so every row carries a sizeClass and the test derives each row's allowed error from it. 'text' is regular-weight text 11 px and larger (the 14 px name, the 11 px detail line), 'caption' is regular-weight 10 px (group entry count, footer lines, Sources count). The 15 caption rows here were captured 2026-09-21 while those sites were still regular; D-RUNG-14 made four of them BOLD the same day, so these rows are the BEFORE state and the bold-caption class still has zero rows of our own, 'bold-caption' is bold 10 px. It had no rows of ours until 2026-09-21, when D-RUNG-14 made four caption sites bold and they were measured under headless cage: errors -0.0007 to -0.054 against a model of 6.2384, where the SAME sites at regular weight measured -0.79. Bold does not render 'more accurately' -- a thicker stroke simply gives the peak-pixel method fully-covered pixels to find, which is the same mechanism behind every other class here, 'glyph' is the 28 px empty-state glyph and the bar glyph. A caption row is allowed tolerance.captionRel times its measured value, because 10 px regular strokes never reach full coverage and the shortfall scales with the ratio (0.17 to 0.79 on the 2026-09-21 rows, 11 to 13 per cent); every other class is allowed tolerance.abs, which is maxAbsError and was not raised. A row without a known sizeClass is refused by the test, not defaulted.
knownDeviationNote: No row carries knownDeviation any more, and that is the RESULT, not an omission. F-CAL-2 was pinned as a cursor-fill surface effect; it was never one. Under the product owner's ruling of 2026-09-21 -- sample the LONGEST available string at each site and record it -- all 16 text rows on the four re-measurable themes were re-measured on 2026-09-22 and every one lands inside the text class's 0.15, worst 0.1359. The earlier rows had been measured on short strings, where the peak-pixel method under-reads because few pixels are ever fully covered. A future row that genuinely deviates is pinned here by name with its id.
siteNote: Several sites share one {theme, surface, alpha} key, so they share ONE model prediction and carry DIFFERENT measured values - that spread is the point, not a duplication: it is how much the same arithmetic varies across real glyph runs at one size. A row without a site predates the 2026-09-21 top-up. The four caption sites measured that day (group count, scope label, footer status, footer verbs, sources count) all hold within tolerance.captionRel, the tightest being catppuccin sources count at 0.78 against an allowance of 0.819 - so F-CAL-1's relative rule is now evidenced by 15 caption rows across four sites rather than by three rows at one site.

envNote: Every row records the environment that rendered it, 'live' (the user's real session) or 'cage' (a nested headless cage compositor running the dev harness). Provenance per row is right regardless of whether the two differ -- and whether they differ is UNKNOWN, see methodLimitNote. The claim that once stood here, that the difference is confined to glyph rasterisation and is measured rather than assumed, is withdrawn: it rested on three rows that turned out to be a different BUILD, not a different environment, and on a statistic that cannot resolve the question. Tolerance is drawn per (sizeClass, env) pair and an unlisted pair is refused, which is still the right shape -- a class that has earned a tolerance in one environment has not automatically earned it in the other -- but the pairs now hold the SAME tolerance wherever the evidence does not distinguish them. The rule that survives untouched: a design decision may only be certified against live rows, because cage is a test convenience and nobody looks at it.
buildNote: Every row records the BUILD that rendered it, and this field exists because `env` was not enough. F-CAL-3 was filed as a difference between headless cage and the live display. It was not: the live pass measured a shell that had never loaded the build it believed it was measuring. `manifest.json` sets `keepLoaded: true`, so the overlay stays mounted across a hot reload and `omarchy plugin update` -- which ends in `rescanPlugins`, not a restart -- left the pre-bold component instantiated. Proven from the journal rather than argued: the boot the pass ran in logs warnings at Guide.qml[2670 and [2676, the 0.7.1/0.7.2 line numbers, and NEVER at [2823, which is where 0.7.3's MouseArea sits and where the current shell's warnings land. Three rows recorded that morning as live bold-caption were regular-weight 0.7.2 renders and have been removed, not relabelled: their surface was never recorded either, so nothing about them is worth keeping. A bold-caption row on a build known to lack the bold is now refused by a check.
methodLimitNote: WHAT THIS METHOD CAN AND CANNOT SEE. The peak-pixel statistic takes the single most distant pixel from the modal background over a whole glyph run. That is a MAX, so it saturates: as soon as ONE pixel is fully covered it returns the 8-bit arithmetic composite exactly, and every measured peak here is the floor or ceiling rounding of that one number. Two consequences the earlier passes missed. First, the resolution is one least-significant bit of a channel -- about 0.05 ratio points on these backgrounds -- so a figure quoted to four decimals, like D-RUNG-14's '-0.0007', is about a hundred times finer than the instrument. Second, the statistic is a THRESHOLD DETECTOR for 'did a stem land on the pixel grid', and is blind by construction to hinting, subpixel positioning and scale. It therefore cannot establish that two renderings differ, and equally cannot establish that they agree. No valid cross-environment comparison of the same glyphs has ever been made here, in EITHER direction. What the statistic does support is a saturation claim: a peak that equals the composite byte-exact means that run reached full coverage somewhere. The quantity a reader actually experiences is the coverage DISTRIBUTION, which nothing here has measured.
